# c4factory Helm chart

Installs the whole C4 Factory: the operator, its CRDs and RBAC, the admission
policy (a Project is named after its namespace), the read-only UI, and Gitea,
seeded with the tagged templates, with its `base` and `go` CI runners. A device
installs [Agent Sandbox](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox)
itself, first. The Kind test environment installs with kustomize and `make`
instead (`make gitea seed deploy`); this chart is how a device installs it.

Most of it is generated by `make chart` (kubebuilder's helm plugin) from
`make build-installer`'s output. `templates/ui/`, `templates/gitprovider/`, `templates/gitea/`,
`values.yaml` and `templates/NOTES.txt` are written by hand and survive a
regeneration; `Chart.yaml` is never overwritten.

## Install

[docs/getting-started.md](../../docs/getting-started.md) walks a device from
here to a first app the factory builds: the install below, the agents' Claude
token, a model, an Agent and a Crew, and a Gitea issue they turn into a merged
pull request.

1. **Agent Sandbox.** The operator runs its agents in Sandboxes and won't start
   without the `Sandbox` kind:

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/releases/download/v1.0.4/sandbox.yaml
   ```

2. **Project namespaces.** Each project lives in a namespace of its name; make
   the ones you list in `gitea.projects`:

   ```bash
   kubectl create namespace webshop
   ```

3. **The release.** On a fresh cluster Gitea's image may still be pulling when
   the seed starts, so give `helm install` time:

   ```bash
   helm install c4-factory oci://ghcr.io/jairjosafath/c4factory/charts/c4-factory --version VERSION \
     -n c4-factory-system --create-namespace --wait --timeout 10m \
     --set 'gitea.projects={webshop}'
   ```

The release requests about 1.1 CPU and 1.4 GiB of memory on top of
Kubernetes' own, most of it Gitea and the `go` runner; on a two-CPU node, lower
`runners.go.resources` or turn the runner off (`runners.go.enabled=false`).

That is the whole factory. Gitea runs in namespace `gitea`, at
`http://gitea.gitea.svc.cluster.local:3000` inside the cluster; the seed Job,
a hook after every install and upgrade, pushed the tagged templates to
organization `templates`, made organization `webshop`, stored its token in
Secret `webshop/gitea-credentials` and made Project `webshop` (only when the
namespace had none; it never changes one), and the chart made GitProvider
`webshop/gitea` from it. In `webshop` the chart also made the catalog, each
template the seed pushed pinned to its tag (`kubectl -n webshop get
c4catalog`), and Agents `planner`, `designer`, `reviewer` (Opus) and
`implementer` (Sonnet) on the release's `agent-go` image. The Agents read
Secret `webshop/claude-credentials`, key `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (from
`claude setup-token`), which you make; the chart holds no token. Describe the
app in a Brief (the UI's box) and the planner writes the model, or apply your
own Systems and Containers to `webshop`; either way their repositories appear
in Gitea. The admin's password is in
Secret `gitea/gitea-admin`, which Gitea's pod made with a random password on
its first start (the chart renders no credential):

```bash
kubectl -n gitea get secret gitea-admin -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d; echo
kubectl -n gitea port-forward service/gitea 3000:3000   # http://localhost:3000
```

To rotate the admin's password or the runners' registration token, delete
its Secret and restart the pods that use it; Gitea's pod makes a new one:

```bash
kubectl -n gitea delete secret gitea-admin     # or gitea-runner
kubectl -n gitea rollout restart deployment/gitea
kubectl -n gitea rollout restart deployment/gitea-runner-base deployment/gitea-runner-go  # after gitea-runner
```

With `gitea.admin.existingSecret` the admin is your Secret: change its
password there and restart Deployment `gitea`.

A new project later: create its namespace, add it to `gitea.projects` and
`helm upgrade` with the same values. `helm uninstall` keeps namespace `gitea`
and Gitea's volume, so the repositories survive a reinstall; delete the
namespace to drop them.

### Private images

The chart and the images on GHCR are private until the owner makes them
public. A device pulls them with a GitHub token that has `read:packages`
(`gh auth refresh -s read:packages`, then `gh auth token`). Helm pulls the
chart, so log it in first, whichever way the images come:

```bash
gh auth token | helm registry login ghcr.io -u "$(gh api user -q .login)" --password-stdin
```

The images come in one of two ways:

- **A pull secret.** Make a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` Secret in the
  release's namespace and in Gitea's, and name it in `global.imagePullSecrets`
  (the UI, Gitea, the seed and the runners) and `manager.imagePullSecrets`
  (the operator):

  ```bash
  for ns in c4-factory-system gitea webshop; do
    kubectl create namespace $ns --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
    kubectl -n $ns create secret docker-registry ghcr --docker-server=ghcr.io \
      --docker-username=USER --docker-password="$(gh auth token)"
  done
  kubectl -n webshop patch serviceaccount default -p '{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"ghcr"}]}'
  helm install ... --set gitea.createNamespace=false \
    --set 'global.imagePullSecrets[0].name=ghcr' \
    --set 'manager.imagePullSecrets[0].name=ghcr'
  ```

  The Secret has to exist before Gitea's pods, so you make namespace `gitea`
  and the chart doesn't (`gitea.createNamespace=false`). The agent images
  (`agent-base`, `agent-go`) run in Sandboxes the operator makes in each
  project namespace, outside the chart, as the namespace's `default`
  ServiceAccount; the `patch` lets them pull with the Secret. Repeat both for
  every project namespace.

- **Kind: load them.** `docker login ghcr.io`, `docker pull` each image at the
  release's version and `kind load docker-image` it into the cluster; no pull
  secret.

A `vX.Y.Z` tag publishes the chart and its images: the *Release* workflow
(`.github/workflows/release.yml`) pushes the chart to
`oci://ghcr.io/jairjosafath/c4factory/charts`, attaches it to the GitHub release
and pushes `ghcr.io/jairjosafath/c4factory/<name>:X.Y.Z` for `operator`, `ui`, `seed`,
the toolchains `base` and `go`, `agent-base`, `agent-go`, `gitea-runner-base`
and `gitea-runner-go` (all `linux/amd64`). A released chart runs its own
version's operator and UI images. From a checkout, `helm install ... dist/chart`
with `--set manager.image.tag=...` and `--set ui.image.tag=...` installs images
you built and pushed yourself.

Every release checks itself: after *Release*, the *Verify Release* workflow
(`.github/workflows/verify-release.yml`) installs that version's chart from
GHCR on Kind, as above, scaffolds the webshop sample's `orders-api`, then
follows [getting-started](../../docs/getting-started.md) up to the first app's
scaffold and an `Idle` Crew (no Agent runs). The
result is on the repository's Actions page (Verify Release, with the evidence
as the run's artifact); a failing release gets an issue titled
`Release vX.Y.Z fails its check`.

## Values

| Value | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `manager.image`, `ui.image` | repository, tag (default `Chart.appVersion`), pullPolicy |
| `manager.args` | the operator's flags (`go run ./cmd --help`); the defaults are the Kind environment's |
| `ui.enabled` | install the UI (default true); `ui.service` and `ui.resources` |
| `ui.allowedHosts` | host names the UI answers besides localhost, for an Ingress in front of it; any other Host is refused |
| `ui.components` | the UI health view's components; an empty namespace is the release's |
| `gitea.enabled` | install Gitea, the seed and the runners (default true); off, `gitProviders` point at a Gitea of your own |
| `gitea.namespace`, `gitea.createNamespace` | Gitea's namespace (default `gitea`) and whether the chart makes it |
| `gitea.image`, `gitea.resources`, `gitea.persistence`, `gitea.config` | Gitea's image, its share of the node, its volume and extra `GITEA__section__KEY` settings |
| `gitea.admin` | the admin's name and email; `existingSecret` for one of your own, else the password is generated |
| `gitea.projects` | project names: an organization, Secret `gitea-credentials`, GitProvider `gitea` and, when there is none, Project `<name>` in each namespace |
| `gitea.seed.image`, `gitea.seed.waitSeconds` | the seed Job's image (default tag `Chart.appVersion`) and how long it waits for Gitea |
| `catalog.enabled`, `catalog.entries` | for each of `gitea.projects`, the catalog entries of the templates the seed pushes (Frameworks, Standards, Compute, Deployments, Connectors), each pinned to its tag in `templates/versions.txt` (default on) |
| `agents.enabled`, `agents.image`, `agents.credentialsSecret` | for each of `gitea.projects`, Agents `planner`, `designer`, `implementer` and `reviewer` on the agent image (default `agent-go`, tag `Chart.appVersion`), reading the Secret you make (default `claude-credentials`) (default on) |
| `agents.standIn` | for each of `gitea.projects`, Agent `stand-in` on the same image: no model and no Secret, it plans from the catalog and makes a scripted change, to show the loop without a token (default on; off with `agents.enabled=false` too) |
| `agents.<role>` | each Agent's `description`, `model` (Opus, Sonnet for the implementer; a Fable model fails the install), `maxRounds`, `timeoutMinutes` and `resources` |
| `runners.base`, `runners.go` | the CI runners: `enabled`, `image`, `resources`, `workSize`, `tmpSize`; `go.goCache` is the node directory of its Go build cache |
| `global.imagePullSecrets` | pull secrets for the UI, Gitea, the seed and the runners; the operator's are `manager.imagePullSecrets` |
| `gitProviders` | more GitProviders to create, each reading a Secret you make (`existingSecret`), below |
| `crd.enabled`, `crd.keep` | install the CRDs with the chart; keep them on uninstall (default) |
| `metrics`, `prometheus`, `networkPolicy` | the generated metrics endpoint, ServiceMonitor and NetworkPolicy |

### Git providers

Each Project namespace needs a GitProvider: where its Containers' repositories
are created. `gitea.projects` makes them for the release's Gitea; for a Gitea
of your own (`gitea.enabled=false`), the chart can create them:

```yaml
gitProviders:
  - namespace: webshop          # must exist
    name: gitea
    provider: gitea
    url: http://gitea.gitea.svc.cluster.local:3000
    owner: webshop              # the organization holding the repositories
    existingSecret: git-credentials
```

The chart renders no Secret: the token is yours, so you make the Secret, with
keys `username` and `token`, before the install:

```bash
kubectl -n webshop create secret generic git-credentials \
  --from-literal=username=c4factory --from-literal=token="$GIT_TOKEN"
```

`gitProviders[].token` and `username` are gone (they put the token in your
values file and in every revision of Helm's release record); a values file
that still sets them fails to render and says what to do.

The CRDs are part of the release, so these are `post-install` and
`post-upgrade` hooks, created once the CRDs exist. Every `helm upgrade` deletes
and recreates them, so a Container scaffolding at that moment may wait a
reconcile for its GitProvider; `helm uninstall` leaves them in place.
